candidates.detail: HairPigment documents melanin, redness and dye channels as shares between zero and one. Its Serde conversion admits only values contained in that range. Public new and dyed instead use f32::clamp. The installed pinned Rust core source and official Rust documentation specify that clamp retains a NaN input, so new(NaN, finite) retains a nonfinite share and dyed([NaN, 1, 1]) retains a nonfinite first dye channel. For finite ordinary inputs the existing clamping is intentional; infinities clamp at the bounds. No constructor, serializer, hair material, UI or product code was executed.
candidates.consumer_and_safeguards: For a finite default pigment with the NaN dye example, HairPigment::color passes that dye to HairMaterial::base_color. The source computes a finite base from the default finite melanin/redness and multiplies its first component by the retained NaN tint, producing a nonfinite first color component by IEEE arithmetic. Selected preview material, color swatch and offline atlas code consume pigment.color; the actual picker values, rendering, encoding and player-visible effect are not established. Named presets and authored dye constants inspected in the studio are finite, and the separate Serde range conversion rejects NaN if a format supplies one.
candidates.connected_scope: HairPigment programmatic and serialized admission, finite/clamped shares and dye, HairMaterial conversion, UI color selection, preview material and offline texture export.
candidates.proposed_repair: After exhaustive discovery and separate implementation authorization, choose one explicit finite-input policy for all HairPigment constructors and mutators, preserving intended clamping for ordinary finite values and the existing supported named and undyed modes. Propagate any contextual error through real programmatic callers; do not invent a silent fallback without policy.
